rēsponsĭo , ōnis, f. respondeo.
1. An answer, reply; a refutation (rare but class.; “syn. responsum): in quo erat accusatoris interpretatio indigna responsione,” Cic. Balb. 16, 36 ; Gell. 12, 12, 1: “responsio mollis frangit iram,” Vulg. Prov. 15, 1 .— In plur., Plaut. Most. 3, 1, 63.—
2. In rhet.: sibi ipsi responsio, a replying to one's own
argument, Cic. de Or. 3, 54, 207; Quint. 9, 1, 35; 9, 3, 90 (cf.: “ut quasi ad interrogata sibi ipse respondeat,” Cic. Or. 40, 137 ).
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
